title: Se pasiva / impersonal: formación del Estado

sections.content: State-building is a natural fit for the se-passive: institutions were organized, authorities were established, an option was chosen, a federation was formed — a process too collective and improvised to credit to one person. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Después de 1821, se organizaron administraciones desde cero.
items.english: After 1821, administrations were organized from scratch.

items.spanish: Se establecieron autoridades locales y regionales en todo el nuevo territorio.
items.english: Local and regional authorities were established across the new territory.

items.spanish: En Centroamérica se optó inicialmente por una solución federal.
items.english: In Central America, a federal solution was initially chosen.

items.spanish: En 1823 se formaron las Provincias Unidas del Centro de América.
items.english: In 1823, the United Provinces of Central America were formed.

sections.content: A whole paragraph of se-passive verbs in a row (se organizaron, se establecieron, se optó, se formaron) reads as a checklist of everything a new state had to figure out at once — useful when the text wants to convey how much was happening simultaneously, not in a tidy sequence.
